body.statement: Let \(U\sim\mu_{\square}\) be independent of a binary regime label. The maps in \(\mathrm{def:quadratic\text{-}counterexample}\) satisfy the displayed hypotheses of RibeiroSanthirasekaramGlocker2025DynamicOT, Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11: \(d=2>1\), the source is continuous uniform on \([0,1]^2\) up to its null boundary, each target has a strictly positive bounded density on the bounded open convex support \(A_j\Omega_{\square}\), and each \(F_j\) is a time-one dynamic optimal-transport map of a Lipschitz displacement flow. Yet \(\det(\operatorname{sym}(A_1A_0^{-1}))=-7/81<0\). At \(u=(1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}\), for \(z=(-2/9,1/18)^{\mathsf T}\), both endpoints lie in \(\Omega_{\square}\) and \[\langle F_1(u+z)-F_1(u),F_0(u+z)-F_0(u)\rangle=z^{\mathsf T}A_1A_0z=-7/324<0.\] The failure persists on an open SPD-matrix neighborhood. Thus the separate Brenier conditions do not imply the Euclidean strict-monotonicity conclusion in equations (13) and (72).
body.justification: The exact rational calculation supplies a robust admissible counterexample and separates Euclidean positivity from positivity in a state-dependent metric.
body.gap: The exact NeurIPS proceedings Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11, equations (13) and (72), conclude strict Euclidean monotonicity under the displayed Markovian dynamic-OT assumptions; this square-supported displacement-flow witness satisfies them and corrects the implication.
body.consumer: Dynamic-transport counterfactual pipelines obtain a falsification example and a corrected condition before interpreting cross-regime matches as rank preserving.
